utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Before the Prosecution resumes its cross-examination, I'd like to inform the parties, since it was a matter discussed yesterday in court, that the Chamber has given some guidance to the Prosecution this morning in respect of the questions raised. And since the Defence has expressed its concerns about what the Prosecution asked, the Chamber deems it proper to inform the Defence of the guidance given. The guidance basically comes down to that the -- it's the Prosecution that will decide, but keeping in mind that the Chamber at the end of the trial does not evaluate the evidence in isolated bits and pieces, but as a whole. And that it is, therefore, keeping this in mind for the Prosecution to decide whether thinks that it is useful to spend time allocated for cross-examination on confronting witnesses with evidence that has been previously presented to the Chamber, and the Chamber also calculated that the Prosecution has well over one hour left to cross-examine the present witness. Mr. Ierace, are you ready to resume the cross-examination of the witness? Then, Mr. Usher, would you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. DP14, may I remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration that you have given at the beginning of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, might the witness be shown Exhibit D1793.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Ierace: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness. I would like to draw your attention to some features of the map in front of you. Do you see on the map various blue lines which are broken? If so, would you please point to one of those lines.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Witness runs the pointer along the broken blue line that runs diagonally across the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that indicate a creek or creek bed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it indicates a stream.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you see on the right-hand side of the map another similar line, if so, please point to it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Further to the right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Witness indicates blue line above the legend.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see another line in the top left-hand corner of the map, if so, please point to it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Witness does so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, coming back to the area of the bottom left quarter of the map, in particular, the roads marked in yellow, we see that the creek crosses or the stream crosses those roads. Please point to where the stream crosses the roads in the bottom left-hand corner of the map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, and a little higher, I think it crosses some roads again.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And do we also see the symbol for a stream on the bottom of the map just to the right of the centre, to the right of the words "Kobilja Glava." Please point to it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, will you please come back to the dot, that is the red dot which is indicated at the number 4. And point to it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. To the right of the dot we see a yellow line running approximately up the map. Would you please run the indicator along that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Witness does so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I suggest to you that that road followed a ridge. Do you agree or disagree?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you now please place your pointer on the red dot indicated by a "9."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And move the pointer to the left and upwards until you come across a road and leave it on the road.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Further.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Stop. Did that road also follow a ridge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we have the creek or the stream with ridges on either side, that is the stream that crosses the road where you earlier indicated; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I draw your attention to the horizontal and vertical blue lines. Would you please point to one of those.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you see that those lines are divided into 10 spaces, 10 equal spaces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you acquire some familiarity with reading maps in the course of your duties during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you understand that the grid marks on a map are usually 1 kilometre apart?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever heard that said, that the grid lines on a map indicate distances of 1 kilometre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends on the scale of the map, I guess.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at red dot marked number "4" and the black dot --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, to the extent that Mr. Ierace is going to continue in this manner, I think that he should specify because we have all noticed it, that the horizontal spaces are not the same as the vertical ones. So could we be precise and could it be said whether we are talking about horizontal spaces which are more, about two times larger than the vertical spaces.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, that would have been appropriately expressed in the absence of the witness. I wish to respond to it. Could I do so in the absence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Usher, could you ask the witness to leave the court for a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. President, there has been evidence in the Prosecution case in relation to this map and others that the grid references indeed represent the distance of a kilometre, and that the rectangles, thus created, are not square because of the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. obvious factors which apply to any map. None of that evidence has suggested that the indications of a kilometre, whether horizontally recorded or vertically recorded are incorrect, rather one must take care when measuring the distance between two spots on the map, to take that into account. In other words, if one measures a distance between two points on the map which are either vertical or horizontal, then it yields an accurate reading. But if one measures distances which are diagonal, then one must make an allowance for the difference between the horizontal and vertical indications. None of that evidence, as I recollect it, was challenged by the Defence. And, therefore, Mr. President, I take that evidence as having been accepted or at least not challenged, and, therefore, open to acceptance by the Trial Chamber in due course, and for that reason, I propose to continue with this line of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, before -- while giving you an opportunity to respond, you said that the horizontal spaces were about two times larger than the vertical spaces. I noticed that it has been discussed before, that the squares are not really squares but really rectangles and twice the size. That sounds new to me, but please explain it and respond to what Mr. Ierace said.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'd like it if Mr. Ierace could tell us what these obvious elements are that he has spoken of, they are not obvious for us. I would like to say that we have always contested this map with regard to principle, as a matter of principle, we have always said that it is very dangerous to provide a map which is computerised in a certain sense. And we all lose our bearings. I think I was very clear about this, and one can't say that we have accepted this map because one of our requests was to reject it as evidence because it was not sufficiently precise and as a result there were irregularities in it. If I have understood what the Prosecution has told us, we can work with this map, only by taking the vertical and horizontal references and the diagonal wouldn't be a reference we could use. We think that this isn't very logical, but the only thing I would like to know is, what space is the Prosecution talking about? Because the horizontal space is obviously far greater than the vertical space, that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I can give an example, Mr. Hinchliffe gave evidence that the distance between the red dot number 14 and the dot in the centre of the red circle was approximately 1100 metres, and he calculated that off this map. There was no challenge to that. He also gave evidence that the distance between red dot 4 and the central of the red circle was 940 metres, that being a distance that he recorded, that he established with his laser method. When one compares that to the relevant divisions on the longitude marks, one sees that that reading is entirely consistent, in other words, that there are approximately 9 and a half spaces. Mr. President, again we have the problem of ambush by the Defence in the sense that evidence is led by the Prosecution and not challenged and in the Defence case it is suddenly an issue. In my respectful submission it is entirely appropriate for the Prosecution to challenge the evidence that he has given as to distances by referring him to a map, specifically, Mr. Piletta-Zanin continues to express lack of understanding as to why the longitudinal measurements should be shorter than the latitudinal measurements. We have heard explanations in the Prosecution case as to why that is so, that that is something which emanates from depicting a map on a flat surface, that is the surface of the earth in a flat dimension when of course it is on a sphere. In order to -- the evidence has been that in order to calculate a measurement, it doesn't matter whether the map is enlarged or reduced because along with the enlargement and the reduction, one still has the indicators on the latitude and longitude to guide one in determining distance. To put it simply, one of the units which appears longitudinally indicates 100 metres. One of the units indicated latitudinally also equals 100 units. It is accurate if you are measuring spots which are either horizontal or vertical but not diagonal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The -- Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I think that it is perhaps the time to address the question, not only of this map, to decide on this is question on the issue of all the other maps. Because have I understood the matter correctly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you objected against the question, Mr. Ierace responded. You have responded, Mr. Ierace then responded again. Now it is time for a decision. If you want to raise a general issue on maps, the Chamber has invited the parties quite some time ago to agree on maps, and to give one stand up map that would serve the Chamber. Up to that moment, the Chamber will have to find its way through different kinds of maps and to make its -- finally will make its own determinations on the basis of what has been presented as evidence to the Chamber. Mr. Ierace is allowed to continue to question the witness about also on the basis of this map which originally was introduced by the Prosecution, then was introduced as far as this witness is concerned, by the Defence, but it should be -- everything should be perfectly clear to this witness. So if there are any problems in reading this map, it should never result in the witness being misled by these problems. Mr. Usher, would you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, quite simply, I would like to say so as not to lead the witness into error because it is rare to find maps with spaces which are the same, but at the same time are not the same, if I have understood the Prosecution. Maybe the Prosecution could clarify this matter, for the witness, in order to prevent him from being confused because it wouldn't be good to provide him with a map on which the spaces appear to be the same, but, in fact, are not the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think I invited the Prosecution to take care that no confusion will arise. Please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. DP14, we had to discuss a procedural issue in your absence. Sometimes that is necessary and I know it is not pleasant for you, and I thank you for your patience. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I want you to accept from me, hypothetically, that the latitude marks on this map are divided in spaces indicating 1 kilometre, and then further subdivided into 10 spaces indicating 100 metres each. I also want you to accept that the same applies to the longitudes. In other words, when you look at the blue squares each side indicates -- is equivalent of 1 kilometre, subdivided with the small markings into units of 100 metres. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look, if you will, at the distance between the red dot indicated number 4 and the black dot in the centre of the red circle, and please count -- thank you -- please count the spaces of 100 metres between those two points.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nine. 9.3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, look, if you will, at point 14, that is red dot 14 and the, again, the dot in the centre of the red circle. Do you agree that that is approximately, and I stress approximately, 11 of those spaces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, look at the red dot 9 and the dot in the centre of the red Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. circle. Would you agree that the distance is less than the distance between the red dot 4 and the dot in the centre of the red circle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, that completes cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace. Is there any need to re-examine the witness? Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have a few questions I would like to ask. Re-examined by Mr. Piletta-Zanin:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I didn't ask you this question, and I will put the question to you now because we are interested in the layout. In point 9 that you have on the map, could you point to it, please by using the pointer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You spoke about a rock a minute ago. Could you point to these rocks again on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: -- perhaps Mr. Piletta-Zanin could give a transcript reference to the rock.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you please do so, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spoke about a ridge not long ago. A ridge, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you point it out to us, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thanks. This area that you have pointed to, and since this map doesn't really show -- or doesn't really have the indications you usually find, what was the nature of this area? Was it bare, was it a forested area, what kind of area was this?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, this question does not arise out of cross-examination, that is, the nature of the terrain on the ridge. And whilst I am on my feet, for the benefit of the transcript, the ridge indicated is the yellow line that passes approximately on the right-hand side of the box with the words in it "sniping incident number 4."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Since specifically attention has been given to the existence of a ridge, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you are allowed to ask questions on that, only in relation to that ridge. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With regard to this ridge, could you please tell me what the nature of the terrain was in relation to this ridge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the asphalt road up until the -- up to the peak of Orahov Brijeg, and this can be seen on the map, but there is a difference in altitude which is quite substantial. And even at the point that I am pointing to now, the highest difference in altitude is at this point with regard to the asphalt road. And then this curve which is fairly straight -- well, what I am trying to say is that the difference in altitude is great between the point I am pointing to now and the road. And this road down here, it is at least 4 metres below this road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You have spoken about the layout, the topography, I would like to ask you about the nature of the terrain.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That should be reflected in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. I didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: It should be reflected in the transcript, the various points indicated by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness indicated that the one point was a 4 -- approximately 4 to 5 metres lower, I think he said 4 to 5 metres lower. He pointed at the red dot number 9, compared with the road with number 18 on it, which would be the higher road compared to the red dot. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, he also indicated that the portion of the road that cuts through the box, that is the portion beneath the box was higher than the portion which appears above the box.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I think that's what the witness said. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, during the cross-examination several questions were put to you about the distance. I want to ask you the following: With regard to each of the incidents that we have pointed out on this map, I can see the number 4, 9, and 14 here, what can you tell us about the distance on the ground, that is to say, if one takes into account the difference in altitude? Have you understood my question?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And your objection is based on?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Well to the extent that I understand the question, the witness was asked in examination-in-chief what he thought the distances were. This question simply revisits that. The fact that the witness is being cross-examined about distances does not entitle the Defence to re-ask the same questions it asked in chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I ask you, when you told us when examined by Defence counsel of the distances between the red circle and the other red dots, did you take into consideration that there is a difference in height as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please move to your next point, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. This, Mr. President, we need to go into closed session, and I will explain why. Mr. President, your Chamber asked questions in respect of a photograph, and these were precise questions with relation to the wood, and we think that perhaps we could do that. The exhibit is P3261.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We will turn into closed session -- yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, again I don't see how this comes out of cross-examination. No questions have been asked about that photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I take it that you used the photographs to ask questions, perhaps with the use of these photographs, but not directly related to the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I'd like to ask are questions in relation to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that questions will be related to cross-examination as such, the use of a photograph which was not used during cross-examination is not forbidden in that respect, but we'll first turn into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. DP14, I've got a few questions for you. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My first question is: When you first were in contact with Ms. Prodanovic, what did you then discuss during these conversations?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We only discussed whether I would agree to come and testify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Did you discuss with her the content of your testimony or did you do that only later when you arrived in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't discuss the contents until the first time I saw Ms. Pilipovic, that was in August, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- if you did not discuss with her at all your testimony, what was there to invite you to be a potential witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We spoke about the areas I was in, the part of the battlefield I was in where I fought all the time, and whether I would agree to be a witness in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you did discuss the content of your testimony to the extent that you had discussed where you had been, what was the area in which you served?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. You told us that it was surprising that the tank was at Zuc hill at the 850 metre position. Could you tell us why it surprised you or why it was surprising or...

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up until then, they had used tanks, mostly from what we call a safe distance. On this occasion, the tank was at the frontlines and this surprised me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then you have told us about mortars being fired from different positions by the opposite forces. Did you ever experience mortars being simultaneously fired from different positions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the course of the offensive in December 1993, shells rained down. And in that situation, it is very difficult to have the time to think about where they are coming from. But judging by the intensity and the number of shells that fell over those days, there is no doubt that several mortars were involved, not just one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I apologise for interrupting. I wonder if that date of December 1993 is what the witness intended, the year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When you referred to December 1993, were you actually referring to December 1992? Because that's --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then could you tell the Chamber, Blagovac, was that in territory held by the other armed forces or by your armed forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under our forces all the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and is the same true for Krivoglavci -- I am sorry for the pronunciation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Krivoglavci. I don't know what that refers to. I'm not familiar with this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is in one of the documents. It says Krivoglavci. Krivoglavci.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the same as in the case of Blagovac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. May I take you back to the map you have seen several times, the map with the red circle. The area of the red circle, do you have specific knowledge of that specific place, or do you have a general knowledge of that area or no knowledge at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On several occasions, at least 50 times, I was in this area. And when I say "this area" I am referring to the positions and the houses in front of Orahov Brijeg. I think these are the houses: Tica, Jagodici and then Mocevici, Sucur. That is how we called the trenches too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said positions in the houses. We see on the map something that could depict a structure within the red circle. Was there any position in that house in the red circle held by your forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the positions I have mentioned were a little below this position. And whether this house, which is in this circle, actually exists, I couldn't say. But I know about the houses next to which there were trenches. They weren't in the houses because the position of Orahov Brijeg is a dominant position in that area, didn't make it possible for the soldiers to be billeted in those houses. The trenches had been dug next to them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say that you do not actually know whether this structure in the centre of the red circle is a house existing. Did you ever go to that area? I mean, why are you hesitating on whether this is a house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were houses behind our lines too. I used this road going upwards on several times -- on several occasions. There are houses on both the left and the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you go into these houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not into the houses behind the lines. As far as the houses at the lines are concerned, yes, I went into the trenches.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the houses -- there seems to be two -- one or two houses within the red circle. Have you ever entered in one of these houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You yesterday answered a question about the line of sight from that position to other positions. What would be the precise source of your knowledge if you would not have been in these houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was speaking about the field of vision, about what I saw, about where I had been. In the houses, well, I think the line was a little below them and the difference in altitude is perhaps 1 metre or so, and this is from a position that I was present at on several occasions. I observed the same terrain from significantly more elevated positions, and I am convinced that this asphalt road can't be seen, not the entire road can be seen from a single point if you look from the north, not from a single point, regardless of how far north you go, in relation to this red circle

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then my -- if there was combat activity at night, how would you find your targets? I am asking you because of the dark.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had what we could call designated targets and it depended upon who was asking for support and it depended on what was being requested. And depending on this, we would act or rather the -- I was the company commander in Zuc and I asked for assistance. I knew what the targets were. I knew the number of targets in front of my lines. I knew the artillery targets on the basis of their numbers, and for certain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So you had the number of the artillery targets. Would that mean that after dark there would be no small arms fire any more?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. From -- a soldier himself would very often open fire from small arms in response to a hissing sound or any kind of suspicious sign or sign that he found suspicious.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much for your answers to my questions. Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, might I ask one question which goes to the spelling of the house names that the witness referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I have not looked at the transcript. I don't know whether there is any unclarity. Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. Further cross-examination by Mr. Ierace:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told the President a few minutes ago that at least 50 times you were in the area of the red circle and you said: "I think these are the houses, Tica, Jagodici, and then Mocevici, Sucur" and so on. Could you please spell the name of the first house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that they called them Tica houses. T-I-C-A.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. Nothing further, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. DP14, this concludes your testimony in this court. I would like to thank you for coming a long way to The Hague and to answer the questions both of the parties and of the Bench and also for your patience. Once again, thank you very much. And I will ask the usher to escort you out of the courtroom. I hope you have a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, the next name that appears on your list, the list asks for pseudonym and face distortion. I have understood that this is a mistake, and that no protective measures are sought for your next witness. Is that correct? I am not mentioning the name --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So but before calling your next witness, we would first have to go through the documents. Madam Registrar, could you please assist us.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1791, under seal, pseudonym sheet; Exhibit D1792, map marked by witness; Exhibit D1792A, map marked by witness; Exhibit D1793, map of sniping incident number 4, marked by witness; Exhibit D1405, letter dated 10/12/1992 from Trifunovic, Miladin; Exhibit D1406, letter dated 08/12/1992 from Trifunovic, Miladin; D1407, letter dated 06/12/1992 from Trifunovic, Miladin; and D1405.1, English translation; D1406.1, English translation; D1407.1, English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, with respect to D1405, 1406, and 1407, and the respective English translations of those documents, Prosecution is aware that it goes to the issue of weight and not admissibility, but these are among the documents which come from a collection of documents to which the Prosecution has previously raised concerns with respect to authenticity and for the record, we would indicate once again that these three documents fall into the same category, again fully aware that it goes towards weight and not admissibility, however, for the record, we wish to put that matter before the Trial Chamber. And also the Prosecution would object to these documents on the grounds of relevance. They seem to have, in the Prosecution submission, no relevance to the specific charges for which the accused is standing trial. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, could the Defence please respond to it. I think the cautions expressed -- the concerns expressed as to the authenticity --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may answer to that as well, but at least that the irrelevant issue is properly addressed. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace -- Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Regarding the first element, I can see that this is about weight. The weight is easy to find because here we are speaking about a tank. And I think that everyone knows the Prosecution presented its case as being that of a party that was under siege, that was under attack, that had no weapons, being attacked by the other party. But the more our case progresses, the more tanks we find and we find them closer and closer to the lines where they shouldn't really be at all. So whatever the author and the nature of this document, it comes to corroborate the witness's testimony saying -- who said that, I knew there were two tanks, one was in this place and the other one was active somewhat at a distance. Now, the second element I believe that I can respond, and that's regarding relevance, and the relevance, as far as we are concerned, that is to establish the reality of facts of heavy weapons of the other side, and Mr. President, particularly, and I want to state this because Prosecution didn't state this, is that some of the testimonies, some of the statements that the Prosecution presented, they do not -- they are not quite conform with reality, and we intend to call these people to testify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any intention to call the -- to call the authors of the reports? Because this witness knows who it is and this witness, of course, did not --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not that we know of, Mr. President. The people that I was talking about, not the authors, I was really talking about the witnesses of the Prosecution, because the Prosecution wanted to re-open some investigations and this is where this could lead us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The -- all the documents mentioned are admitted into evidence. The pseudonym sheet, under seal. Is the Defence ready to call its next witness? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we are, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon. I take it that you are Vaso Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before giving evidence in this court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. May I invite you to make that declaration and the text will be handed out to you now by Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated, Mr. Nikolic. Ms. Pilipovic, please proceed. Mr. Nikolic, you will first be examined by counsel for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Examined by Ms. Pilipovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Nikolic, good afternoon. 2 A. Good afternoon. 3 Q. Mr. Nikolic, you told us your full name and last name. Can you 4 give us some more personal data, where and when were you born?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I was born in Bosnia-Herzegovina, a place called Ugljevik 10th of April, 1961.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nikolic. Can you tell us what is your occupation?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I have a third grade of a technical school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us in 1992, where did you live?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In Sarajevo in 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1992, where did you work or were you employed?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was. I worked in Bosna Lijek.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that in 1992 you worked in Bosna Lijek is that -- was that throughout 1992, your employment in 1992?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: My employment ceased on the 3rd of April 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that your employment ceased on the 3rd of April 1992, can you tell us the reason why it ceased?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well unless I am mistaken on the 3rd of April 1992, it was a Thursday or a Friday, I lived in the apartment of my sister's in Sarajevo in the city centre itself. That was in Kralja Tomislava Street. Because at that time as I worked in Bosna Lijek and I had been living in Sarajevo since 1977, I socialised would people so in some way I felt fear that we can't. And just in case, I stayed with my sister's, I sheltered there. My sister who was married in Mrkovici belonging to the municipality of Centar, that was some 10 kilometre from Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Nikolic, are you telling us that from that time on you lived in the village of Mrkovici as you say, Centar municipality of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, can you answer, until when did you live in the village of Mrkovici?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I lived in the village of Mrkovici until the 20th of February 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, we are interested in the period from September 1992. Can you tell us, where were you in September 1992?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Throughout this time I was in Mrkovici, and when the conflict broke out on the 6th of April in Mrkovici, I was on elevation 906, Mala Kula.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, I asked you where you were in September 1992, and you told us that from April 1992 you were on elevation Mala Kula?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. And through all the time, throughout this time until Dayton.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us if you were a member of a unit?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. At that time I was a member of Mrkovici company, that's what it was the company called, until the Republika Srpska Army was established in June. Until then I belonged to this company called Mrkovici company. We were self-organised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that you were Mrkovici company and that you were self-organised, can you tell us, what was the reason for your self-organisation?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I told you already, that I arrived from Sarajevo. So I knew only a few people in Mrkovici, that is my sister's relatives, that is my sister's husband's relatives.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, I ask you to answer my questions briefly. I asked you a question about the reason, and was there a reason why you self-organised yourselves? Is there something that happened in Mrkovici on the 6th of April?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: On the 6th of the April, the first murder took place, a man was killed. We were attacked about 1200 hours -- 12.30 hours we were attacked suddenly, and at that time we had the first victim. He was called Nedjo [phoen] Dragas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us who you were attacked by on the 6th of April?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: On the 6th of April we were attacked by the then paramilitary formations, Muslim paramilitary formations, who attacked us suddenly. We didn't think they would. There were no occasions and we were not prepared, and then it turned out that we obviously paid for this by having a casualty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that following the establishment of the Republika Srpska Army, through establishment system, your company, Mrkovici, did it get a different name?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: It was a company. I don't know exactly which one it was, but it belonged to the Hresa Battalion because we changed -- the name of the company changed which was 2nd, 3rd, or 5th. But in any case that happened later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that you were a member of the 2nd or 3rd or 5th company, that it changed its name, can you tell us the positions of your company at the time -- at the time of the conflict, we are talking about September 1992 to August 1994. What were the positions of your company?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Our company held on to the positions of the village of Mrkovici, that is from Debelj until Biosko that is a distance from about 3.000 to 4.000 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, can you tell us, as a member of the company that you say was part of the Hresa Battalion, how many people were members of your company?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Our company had between 70 and 100 men, that depended on people who were injured or were killed. So this number went from 70 to 100.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how were you armed?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Initially we were not well-armed, and then later on when the army was established of the army of Yugoslavia [as interpreted], we got some weapons. And so it was better for us, it was more secure. We got automatic weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there professional servicemen in your company?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: There were not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, I think that you said by the -- when the establishment of the army of Yugoslavia --

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: It is probably a mistake, of the army of Republika Srpska. Because I can see that in the transcript it says of the army of Yugoslavia. So when the Army of Republika Srpska was established.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, you told us that the positions of your company went from Debelj to Biosko --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, it may well be a mistake but it's appropriate for the witness to be asked rather than counsel to assume it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I asked the witness, I suppose I could have asked him, but I perhaps -- perhaps when I was asking the witness, I realised that he had made a mistake. But I could have asked but he had already answered, he said that he had made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but the next question Ms. Pilipovic, I take Mr. Ierace's -- the next question starts with: "You told us that," whereas Mr. Ierace seems to find --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will repeat the question. 48 line 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, in the transcript at page 48 line 24, at least that's the position on my transcript, we have what appears to be an answer, "It is probably a mistake of the Army of Republika Srpska." I think that was in fact said by Ms. Pilipovic, as I understood the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I thought you were talking about the next question. Yes, the question has been answered and I think in 1992, no JNA was established, so I don't really think that this would -- or would you dispute -- would that be in dispute --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Well I am just not clear what it was the witness said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it you refer to one of his earlier answers when he was talking about the creation of the Republika Srpska Army. I think it was not necessary. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: As you wish, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, can you tell us, for the transcript, can you repeat, for the transcript, the positions -- the positions -- the lines of your company?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The defence lines of my company were from the place called Debelj until the place called Gornje Biosko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us about the length of the frontline of your company?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: There length of the front line was about 3.000 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The depth of the area of your company, can you tell us about that?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand. What do you mean by "depth"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, you said that the line, the length was 3.000 metres, three kilometers?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was its depth?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well its depth, it would be very hard for me to fathom because as far as I know, I only know that part of Mrkovici which is 3 to 4 kilometers. I really don't know what was behind us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, at the beginning of your testimony you told us that you were on the positions, I think you said of Mala Kula, did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you elaborate a little about the location of Mala Kula in relation to the positions of your company? What is it, to start with?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The position of Mala Kula on the map is some 120 metres above 906 elevation point. It is an Austrian fortress of about two floors, 100 square metres, it is of the old Austro-Hungarian origin that was building from that time and it was turned towards the village of Mrkovici, so it was completely unfortified and on all sides it was surrounded by a very tall pine forest so it could not be at risk. So it -- Mrkovici could be seen from there and wider area of Kosevo. So the first few days when we got on to that fort, to that tower, we went in in order not to allow the village to be targeted from that tower.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Nikolic, can you tell us, do you know who was the commander of your company, the commanding officer, the commander of your company?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Before the Army of Republika Srpska was established, the commander, the first commander was Veseljko Dragas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you telling us that the commanders changed of the company?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the period from September 1992 until August 1994 what was the situation in your company, speaking of company commanders?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In 1992 in September until 1994 there was one who was -- who -- commander who died and there were another two, another two commanders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, just from my better understanding, the witness has testified several times about elevation point 906. If you want to show later on a map to the witness which -- on which this elevation point appears, I would highly appreciate if you do it now so that at least I can orient myself better and better understand the testimony of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Your Honour, I am going to show the witness a map, and later that will be an exhibit, Defence exhibit, and my co-counsel will ask some questions in relation to the map and the positions on the map, and that will be Defence Exhibit 1794. I think it is the number 4. That is map relating to incidents 8 and 3. We can provide it in colour since we will be using it later, if it is easier, for the purposes of identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As far as I am concerned, Ms. Pilipovic, there is no need for marking, but just to be sure that I understand the witness correctly in what he says.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, when you tell us and clarify about the area you were present in, when you say that this was the Mala Kula area, with the permission of the Trial Chamber I will now show you some photographs that the Defence has.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is document 338. These photographs have been shown to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, just for my -- 906, has that been clarified now or...

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can ask the witness a question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, could you have a look at the map to your right.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. We have colour copies for the Trial Chamber, but I didn't find all of them at the same time. It will be easier and more visible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you show us elevation 906 on this map?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's here.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the sake of the transcript, the witness indicated elevation 906. It is the number which is below the word "Grdonj."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What we have here above is Mala Kula, that's the fortress.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, the point above the word "Grdonj" according to the witness is the place called Mala Kula.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, is the photograph I have provided to the right of you --

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If possible, could you put the photograph on the map. We won't be using it for the moment. And this is so that we can all have a look at the photograph. Mr. Nikolic, do you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's Mala Kula.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this building, the white building that we can see in the photograph is the only building -- is that one building or are there three buildings there, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: It is just one building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The building we can see in this photograph, can you confirm that this building is the one which is marked with a black point, a black dot, on the document, and with regard to the incident 338? So on the map that you had a look at before I showed you the photograph?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I haven't understood you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The black dot that you marked on the map above the word "Grdonj" --

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- is that the building which designates the Mala Kula according to you?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, can you explain in relation to the photograph that we have before us, can you tell us the positions of the Republika Srpska Army were, the positions of your company?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. The first position was in the fortress itself, that's the most prominent point. I don't know how this appears on the monitor. But then it went to the right. It descended and extended as far as Spicasta Stijena, the sharp rock which doesn't appear in the photograph, and then it curves down here towards Debelj. This was our most prominent position, our most prominent point, the Mala Kula.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the transcript, I think I heard something in the plural with regard to this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you know exactly how to do it. That is to ask the witness to repeat an answer, not indicate what you heard. Perhaps ask the witness -- Ms. Pilipovic, you may ask the witness again and certainly Mr. Piletta-Zanin will guide you --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, in relation to the photograph that we have before us, can you show us where the positions of your company were, to the right, right part of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: They can't be seen from here, in this photograph. Because this is a distance of about 50 metres here from the fortress to here. There was just another point here from the fortress, about 50 metres away. And then further on you can't see anything. The sharp rock is there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the sake of the transcript, the witness looked at the map from the right, from the east, and he indicated a position, the positions of the company which extend to the area which the witness called the sharp rock area.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the interpretation and transcription refers to it as a map. It is a photograph. And it says "the witness looked at the map from the right, from the east." It is unclear to me where the photograph is pointed and where the camera is pointed. That would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, I do agree. In order to better understand the testimony of the witness, could you please ask the witness in what direction the camera is pointing so that we have some feeling about what would be east, north, west, or south. If the witness knows.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, in relation to this photograph, can you tell us what direction this building was photographed from, the building you called the Mala Kula? When we look at the photograph, was the lens directed towards the north or to the south? Can you find your bearings in relation to this photograph and explain -- explain the points of the compass, with regard to this photograph? How was this building photographed?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well it is difficult for me to explain this. All I can say is that this is photographed from the direction of the town of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that it is photographed from the direction of the north, if it was photographed from the direction of the town of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether there is a translation problem, it might be, but Ms. Pilipovic, what we hear and what we read in the transcript is that you say: "If it was -- the picture was taken from the north," I understand that to be the lens looking south -- to the south --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- it would be taken from the city of Sarajevo. What, as far as I understand the maps we have seen until now, that if you take a picture from the building that you -- that appears where the witness has said was the Mala Kula, then taken from the north, I have some difficulties in understanding that that would be taken from the direction of Sarajevo. I would have less difficulties if it would say that it is in the direction of Sarajevo, of the city.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, can you tell us what direction, we are talking about the north, west, east, south, from what direction was this photograph taken, according to you, can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: It is difficult. I told you that this photograph was taken from Sarajevo towards Mrkovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if we look from the direction of the town?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, in relation to this photograph can you explain the elevations we can see at the bottom of the photograph? What do these elevations represent?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: These are pine trees that were cut down when the fortress was taken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic I apologise. I have to interrupt you there. I am referring to the part of the elevation that can be seen at the bottom of the photograph, the slight mound at the end of the photograph, right at the bottom of the photograph, if you look in the direction of the north.

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I haven't understood you correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, if this photograph is taken from the city, I take it that it, it is taken from the south of the building. And if you then say that the north is on the bottom of the photograph, I again have difficulties in understanding --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the top of the photograph, Your Honour. I don't know maybe there was a mistranslation. But I was referring to the top of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, at the top of the photograph, the elevations that you can see there?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's clear to me. That is the village of Mrkovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you show us in this upper part whether there are houses that can be seen?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. These are villages here, it extends in this area. That is the village of Mrkovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the sake of the transcript, the witness pointed to the upper part of the photograph in the direction of the building which he marked as Mala Kula; in the central part of the photograph he pointed to the village of Mrkovici. Mrkovici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's what he said that the village was. He was pointing to the area above and on the right-hand side of the building that appears in the photograph where it seems that it's less wood and some meadows up to the top of that hill. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, can you tell us, in your opinion, what is the distance from this fortress to Mrkovici?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: From Kula to the furthest house in Mrkovici, that is about a kilometre and a half, as the crow flies. But it is about two and a half kilometers if you go by path. That would be the house which is furthest away in Mrkovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to...?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Mala Kula.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Nikolic, with regard to -- in relation to Mala Kula, you said that there is a sharp rock to the right?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how far it is, how far the sharp rock is?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: It's about 100 metres to the right of Mala Kula.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I have understood you correctly, your company positions were in the area of the Debelj Biosko place and this building was on the line of your company, the Mala Kula building, and there was the sharp stone too, have I understood you correctly?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, during the conflict from 1992 to 1994, during that period, can you tell me whether you were present in this fortress all the time?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Mostly. Mostly all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to the area of the town of Sarajevo, can you tell us which positions you can see from this fortress, if you can see any?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: From Mala Kula, and it was not possible to see much in the direction of the town of Sarajevo because of the forest. You could see part of Kosevo, Grovo Bala [phoen] and up as far as Zetra. So that is the part of Sarajevo that could be seen.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, the cemetery Bare.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, can you tell us what weapons your company possessed?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Our company had infantry weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any snipers in your company?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No, there weren't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any trenches along the line of your company?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With relation -- in relation to the defence line of your company, can you tell us how far the BH Army frontlines were?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well, it depended on the place. It varied from place to place. Between 30 to 100, 150 metres. It depended on the situation and the layout of the terrain. But on average, between 50 and 100 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the area of the frontline of your company, can you tell us whether you personally knew how BH Army soldiers were armed, what sort of weapons they had?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't think I received any information, but as I participated in the fighting and mounted resistance, I think that for a long period of time during the conflict they possessed weapons which were better than ours. They were armed better than we were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that when you participated in the fighting and when you mounted resistance for back attacks, can you tell us how often there was fighting in the area where your company was deployed?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well, in Mrkovici I think that it was difficult to find a -- to think of a day which passed without any incidents when it was fairly calm during the four-year war period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that it was difficult to single out a day when it was calm, can you tell us what the intensity of the fighting was?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well, it mostly involved daily provocations, fire would be opened. So one would never know when there was an attack or when they had prepared an attack and when they hadn't. It was simply impossible for us to assess. We were provoked regularly from infantry weapons and sometimes from artillery weapons, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "artillery weapons" can you tell us whether you personally know what sort of artillery weapons were used, what sort of artillery weapons did the BH Army used against the positions of your company?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well, from mid-1992 and up until the end of the war they constantly used a tank which was below Zetra, below the sports hall in the tunnel which connected the railway station and the Ciglana settlement and it fired from the tunnel very rapidly and then it would enter the tunnel. That's where they fired from the tank because with regard to the picture the left side of the village, it was a visible for them. They had a good field of vision. They used Howitzers which they position said on the Bare cemetery -- in the Bare cemetery, and they also fired from the Sedrenik area. They fired from mortars and from a Browning.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I am just concerned to the extent which the evidence relates or doesn't relate to the indictment period. Perhaps that could be qualified. The last answer started off with a reference from mid-1992 in relation to a tank. It is not clear whether that applies to the Howitzer. The use of Howitzers as well. It would be appropriate in my respectful submission for the Defence to, where required, clarify whether we are talking about the indictment period or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please ask for some clarification as far as the time period is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I think that the witness was referring to the entire period, but I will repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we could shortcut it. You said something about -- that there was a tank from mid-1992 until the end of the war. The other weaponry that you mentioned, would that cover the same period or would that be limited in time that you know of their existence and their use?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, that refers to the tank. That entire part --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And as far as the other weaponry is concerned? You mentioned Howitzers --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mostly in 1993, the most intense fire came from the Bare cemetery and below Harasno that is to say Sedrenik, they were active throughout the war time period.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, you said that from the Sedrenik area, which was under Hratovo, you said that there were mortars there and a Browning?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what is Browning is?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: It is a heavy infantry weapon. I think its calibre is 12 millimetres. It is used to fire on armoured vehicles and on other vehicles, cars and lorries.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, you told us that in 1993 there was constant firing from the Bare cemetery and from Sedrenik below Hrastovo. And when you say "constantly" with regard to 1993, can you tell us what nonstop means in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: That means that there was never a lull. We spent a lot more time on duty at the line than we spent time resting. We were provoked all the time and we were always prepared for being attacked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1993, were there any days which passed, as far as you know, during which there was fighting which was very intense?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In mid-1993 attacks were mostly launched against the area of that municipality, the municipality of Centar and Stari Grad and especially against our positions. There were so-called manoeuvre attacks that were carried out in order to take away as many forces as possible and to attack somewhere on the other side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, when you have a look to the left, the area of the Mala Kula, so on the left-hand side of the photograph, we can see that a lot of the forest has been destroyed here. And for the period 1992, 1993, and 1994, can you tell us what this area was like? Did it look like this, too?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Up until June, May or June 1993, I think, this area was exactly the same. It was forested. All you have here are the remainders of pine trees which were destroyed by light artillery and recoilless cannons. This is when the BH Army attacked us and when we withdrew from Mala Kula.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spoke about mid-1993. Could you be a little more precise.

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well, I can be precise. I can be more precise. They took Mala Kula on the 14th of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, when you say that on the 14th of June 1993 the BH Army took Kula, you also mentioned a recoilless cannon?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us from which positions -- which positions did they fire from with the recoilless cannon?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well the Mala Kula is not accessible. That is where -- where there is a car now, the recoilless cannon was taken there at night, 1 or 2, I don't know what time any more exactly. Because I was on duty in the small fortress on that evening. And this place here, where the car is, that was the only entrance. There weren't any other entrances to that building. So we were then attacked from the front of this building, and we managed to withdraw behind the building. We had one casualty, and we abandoned the fortress.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, you mentioned fighting in the Mala Kula area. Can you tell us how often there was fighting if we are talking about attacking the Mala Kula and taking it?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: We were constantly provoked at Mala Kula. But it is very well -- it is very firm, so we didn't respond to provocations from infantry weapons because the walls are very thick, 70 or 80 centimetres thick, so in certain sense we were safe and we didn't respond to provocations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you said that on the 14th of June BH Army took the fortress, are you saying it was under BH Army control from the 14th of June?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: For 24 hours I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, you're telling us that there was fighting on the 15th of June as well?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's when we were talking it back, on the 15th or the 16th. It is possible that they stayed there for 24 or 30 hours, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether in the period of 1993 there were other such instances of fighting in respect of your explanation of the attack and the taking of the area around Mala Kula?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: There was in 1993, in April, we lost the Sharpstone feature, two -- that is three, that is two trenches and the observation point were taken in the night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say in April 1993, can you tell us at which time in April of 1993, when did this fighting take place?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: It was middle of the month, that means from the 10th until the end of the month, end of April. There were daily fighting in order to get the Sharpstone feature back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, you are telling us about the fighting in the area of Sharpstone feature. Are you telling us that you, as a member of your company, you also took part in the battle?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Earlier I said that this fort was some 100 metres away from the Sharpstone. When there was a need or if need be, there would be a -- that would lessen the number of people in the Mala Kula. If we needed to deploy them elsewhere in order to return the lost positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, since you are telling us that you participated in the fighting in the area of Sharpstone feature, can you clarify for us, or rather explain about the frontline, what was it like in the area of Sharpstone feature?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The frontline, the Sharpstone -- of the Sharpstone feature, it extended some 200, 250 to 300 metres up to the actual sharp stone. Which just like around the Mala Kula, there was a wooded area there and because of the war, because of the fighting, it was all felled. All the trees were felled. And it was bare. We held on to two trenches in Sharpstone, feature with one observation point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that you held on to two trenches with one observation point on the Sharpstone feature, can you tell us whether you personally were the position of the observation point and if you had been, what were you able to see from that position in respect of the area of the city?
