utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I went to the observation points and in the trenches. From the observation point it is possible to see from the Sharpstone feature the left-hand side -- the left half of Sedrenik up to the cemetery of Bakija. And the second half of Sarajevo across Miljacka which is already Trebevic and Bistrik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what kind of view is it, what were you able to see specifically, for instance, if you are on that observation point?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The observation point is made in such a way because it is located on the Sharpstone feature itself. So it is slightly sloping because of the possibility of bullets. It is on the edge itself in order to observe from the observation point it is possible what I told you. That part of Sedrenik is visible, houses, some 50 houses, all kinds of buildings, facilities, and then to the left you can see Borije, and the neighbouring village, or rather of the neighbouring company, the area of the neighbouring company where it bordered, that is what you can see from the observation point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Nikolic, can you tell us, did you go to trenches in the Sharpstone feature?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what is it possible to see from the trenches?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: You cannot see anything from the trenches because the trenches are connected with the observation point through a connecting trench. So they were connected by cable phone and we would receive instructions from the observation points, from the observers. In relation to the observation point, we were about 1 or two metres inside in our territory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In respect the trenches and your positions on the Sharpstone feature, can you tell us in that area, what was the length of that part where the trenches were?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: About 300 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to where the trenches of your company were, how far were the frontlines of the BH Army in relation to that part?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Their first line in respect of us on the Sharpstone feature was about as high as Sharpstone was, about 50, 60 metres. They were just below the rock, below the Sharpstone. That's where their first frontlines were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say their first frontlines, are you telling us that there were other lines in that area?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: There were three lines in that area of the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In relation to the Sharpstone feature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that there were three lines, can you tell us where about the second line, how far was it in relation to your positions?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: It would be hard to clarify this and give precise details. For the second line it could be some 200 metres to our lines. They were connected with the connecting trench to the third line, and they were -- the third line was in the houses in Sedrenik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe this is time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it is. But I would like to try before having a break to get a better impression of this photograph because I am still a bit confused. Could you please look at the photograph again. You said that you could see, as far as I understand, from this structure in the direction of Kosevo. What direction could you please point with the pointer where you would look if you were looking in the direction of Kosevo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's where Kosevo is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's where Kosevo is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The road on which the car is situated, where does that road go to? Where does it lead you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This road was made after the war. This was the end of the road where the car is. It used to be an old Austro-Hungarian road. It was very narrow and it couldn't be used. Nothing could go there. Where the car is that's where the end is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand. That's where the end is. And if you go the opposite way, where do you end up? I mean, where does this road bring you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nowhere on the road. You can just go down the rocks, down the ridge to the village of Grdonj some 200, 300 metres below. After this car, there is a big slope, a steep slope that goes some hundred metres below.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so where the car is the road ends?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that -- does the road end where the building is? I don't know whether that is the front of the car or the back of the car.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. It passes by and it -- this is where the road goes which collects it to the village of Mrkovici and this is how you can get by car. It goes here below the pine trees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So you say if you would follow that road passing by the building, then the road would lead you to the village of Mrkovici; is that a correct understanding?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And now the elevation point 906, where would that be situated? Could you point in what direction, you said it was quite close to the building, where is elevation point 906, in what direction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 906 elevation point should be about this part here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So we are looking more or less down from elevation point 906 to that fortress; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, before we adjourn, for the transcript, could we record where the witness indicated elevation point 906 was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the elevation point 906 is situated by pointing to it at a spot which is on the right-hand side of the road, seen from the camera position, at a short distance from the car. If the parties would not agree, if I say that it seems to be some 15 metres, then I would like to hear from you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could I just add, Mr. President, that the relevant spot appears white or whitish in amongst the grass.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, there seems to be a bigger stone in the grass just to the right edge of the road. We will then adjourn until five minutes past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my co-counsel will proceed, with your leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Examined by Mr. Piletta-Zanin:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To start with, yes, the witness's microphone is not on. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness to start with, I'd like you to, if you still have it, and I don't think you do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown the map, this map, yes. Thank you. The map that you had earlier. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, perhaps --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Usher, could we please focus on the Grdonj area. Could you focus on the Grdonj area. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness -- thank you, that's right. Can you see two green lines here, one dark, the other light green. They are going around the upper part of the screen, of the map?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, let us assume that on this map, that this map would have had marked positions to the north, VRS positions, and to the south BH Army lines. Would you be able to, if these lines are not correctly marked in, would you be able to mark them in correctly?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand you well. Which lines did you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the moment, I am speaking of the Serb lines, that is, the dark lines. If these lines are not properly positioned, would you be able to trace them properly; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The lines of the Army of Republika Srpska, I would be able to put them in, to trace them, but I am not sure about theirs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Could you please take a black pen. You will be given one. Is it black? I think it is. And could you please draw, Witness, Witness, as far as you can recall, draw the position of the lines the way you think that they were for the Serb side.

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: It would be this part that I am certain about, that's what it was like. That goes from the small fort to the end of the sharp stone. These would be the positions of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please make it a little stronger, the line, a little thicker.

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, now as far as the area located between the line that you just added on this map, and the lines, light green lines, that is the lines that are supposed to show the BH Army lines are concerned, to whom did the area in between belong, if it belonged to anyone?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: This part in between, between this line I drew, that is the defence lines, our defence lines and the BH Army lines were about 50 metres. So about here --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, Witness. I am -- what I am asking you, can you please focus on the question. What I am asking you is not the distance, but the area between the two lines, the line that you just drew and the light green area which is located on the word "Suma." This area here, who was there, if anyone was there, of course?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: That was the area in between. That was no-man's land.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, earlier you spoke of a cannon, and I believe that you called it a Browning cannon, that was positioned just opposite the small fort. I believe that was 12.5 calibre cannon, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I was talking about a Browning, but it is the recoilless cannon that was taken up there. It was a lot stronger and it had a much stronger intensity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. This recoilless cannon, was it positioned opposite the small fort to a location which would have been in front of -- by the car that we saw on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: It would be taken out in the night and it would start firing in the morning. We couldn't see what the distance was, but that was the only area where it could have fired.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. Witness, could you please answer briefly. Now, the area that you have indicated as being 906 elevation, is that where the cannon was, is that what your testimony is?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, you spoke about the recoilless cannon. Is that a weapon which is of a certain weight, technically speaking, what can you tell us about it?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I don't know much about this, but I know it has to be towed by 5 to 10 people. It has to be towed, manually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, therefore, how did Muslim forces, how were they able to get access to the peak of Grdonj?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I don't know the answer to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you confirm that they had access to it?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: They had access to Grdonj. Initially I said there was a small old narrow road, Austrian road, old Austrian road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Witness, now, if you can, can you please indicate with a pointer, I believe that it is in front of you, not with a pen, thank you. With the pointer, can you indicate, you spoke of the second and the third line, and for the third line you said that houses were included in the third line. Could you please tell us, on this map to which houses did you refer to?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: These black dots, if they are houses. So this line went this way. It is hard for me to find my bearings, but this line should go this way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. But you are unable to tell us precisely for certain?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: With difficulty, because on the map I don't have as good as view as I had on the spot itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, the transcript for the recording of where the witness indicated the third line of trenches was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could you please clarify this issue, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you made a gesture earlier, you indicated, but I understand that you are not certain --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that the witness indicated some houses that were under an undulating wavy green line by the inscription which says "Sedam Suma."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you spoke about --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The easiest way would be for the witness to mark it, otherwise --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, marking would avoid any misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President. We do not wish to do that because before Mr. Ierace gets up again and interrupts me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, no. You said you didn't want to -- were you about to put your next question to the witness or --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I wanted to ask other questions and I thought it was useless for him to mark them, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... entirely free to not to ask the witness to mark what he said, but then it should be clear for the transcript. So then --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- if Mr. Ierace would agree with the description, but as far as I remember, the houses pointed at by the witness were two black structures just south to the lower green line and one up and one to the left as well, approximately in the centre of the map. But not only in the centre where Sedam Suma is written, but also more to the right and also a bit lower. Also as far as I remember, in the area which seems to be in the -- which is yellowish coloured with a few black dots in there as well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness -- I withdraw that. You spoke to us about the taking of the small fort. Were there other observation posts, other lines that were taken by the enemy, for you, that was the enemy at the time, and I am talking about the area that you knew; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you show us on this map approximately the areas where lines or positions were taken and if so taken, then returned, taken back by you.

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: On this map I find it very hard to find my bearings. If you look to the right of the map where there is this empty space and above you see that it says Streliste, and this in fact is the Streliste and this here is Sedam Suma. So this map isn't logical to me. And that's why I find it hard to find my bearings because we also have Veliko Kula a large fort and it was above the Sedam Suma because this empty space should have been where the Streliste is. So this map is difficult. And around here there should be our large fort. And it went -- the line went on from there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When you were telling us, we will record it for the transcript, but you said that the observation post that was taken, could you tell us where on the map that was?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: According to this map, that should be about here somewhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In respect of the question asked and following the witness saying that this map was difficult for him, the witness pointed on the "B" of Brdo, I believe. It is a "B" which is half eaten by the top of the map, but it is between the "B" and the "R" of the word Brdo. We see in the top right corner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we focus more to the centre. Could the map be repositioned more to the left so that we can see better.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I am not sure whether Mr. Piletta-Zanin intended to record for the transcript the position of the observation post. That's not clear from his statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think he was describing where the witness said the observation post was located, that it was taken, that is on the dark green line just below the -- between the "B" and the "R."

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: As long as that is clear. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would have to be taught to be -- express myself more clearly because I find it very difficult to express myself more clearly than this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, could you please focus on the lines that you have in front of you on the map, please. With a pointer, can you please indicate the location from the line held by the VRS, what was the direction of the fire as you have known it? That is, what was the direction that the shots were going to? Can you indicate by gestures on the map.

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: This direction was surrounded by the wood up to the Mala Kula. It went on to the beginning of the Sharpstone feature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, Witness, I am going to stop you. From the trenches, when you opened fire could you please draw, with the pointer -- indicate with the pointer the direction of the fire direction of firing. Where were you firing at?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The view of this area in front of us went like this towards Bakija up to the cemetery of Bakija, that's where it looked at.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you please follow my question very closely. I understand what you are indicating, but my question is very simple. Indicate with your pointer on the line that you drew, in the middle of the line that you drew -- no, middle of the line that you drew, that you yourself drew --

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Middle. Thank you. There it is. Stay with your pointer in the middle of the line that you drew.

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Don't move your pointer. I am going to ask you this question: Do you know from this location, was fire opened?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know if the fire was opened?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: This is where the Mala Kula is. This is what I happened holding the pointer at. The fire was opened there during fighting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Now, from there, if you are opening fire in the direction, I think, of the enemy lines, can you please show us the direction of fire with your pointer, when there was fighting?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: From this post, from this location there was no direction of combat. It was only possible when we were attacked that we would then be opening fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, can you please put it on another part of the line from which fire was opened, where you want on that line?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. From there, towards what were you firing, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Firstly, my learned colleague asked the witness whether fire was directed from the Mala Kula, he says no. The next question is effectively when you fired from that area where was it directed. He now invites the witness to indicate where fire was directed from another point on that line without asking first whether fire was directed from that point of line, whether it was surrounded by trees and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could you tell us from where usually in that area fire was opened? I am not talking whether it was response fire or not, but from where you would fire to the opposite army. Could you please point at this point.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The witness points at a line which starts just left from the red circle on the map, through the red circle and then to the right of that red circle just next to it. Could you indicate what the direction of fire was if you fired from the positions you just indicated? In what direction would you fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We were regularly attacked from that direction, and that was the only direction of fire because this part was not visible for us because there is a very large piece in front of Grdonj. So we couldn't see it. This was -- the firing line, firing direction was towards Bakija. This direction and part of the cemetery on Bakija was visible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The witness indicates that the -- they could not fire at the position just south and south-west from the red circle where the, I think on the original map it is greenish, because there were woods, and then the witness pointed to the area south of the red circle, especially where the yellowish features do appear. And he then indicated a line going from the red circle down in the direction of Bakija. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, with all due respect, we do not agree with your description. Since the witness didn't say that he could not fire at this position. What he said is that he couldn't see a position. But as far as the possibility of firing is concerned, the witness clearly said that shots went in that direction, in the direction where you have the word "Sedrenik" because it is from this area that they were the subject of attacks. So I think that the direction of fire is north, north-east in the direction of Bakija, as well. I think this is what the witness said. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I would now like to carry on. What type of weapons did you yourself have, in your unit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I have great difficulties in accepting that the fire went in the north-east direction. I think that, but I will just consult my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please take --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have consulted my fellow Judges and they have confirmed that my description was the right one. But in order to avoid whatever misunderstanding, could the witness be given a red -- I think we are using red -- or is it -- red, yes. A red marker. Would you perhaps first indicate the positions you just indicated on the map from the positions from where you would fire.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could you do that with a red felt pen. No, you earlier indicated from the point you just indicated through the red circle to the other side of the circle. Is that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what you indicated before.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was our line which went through the red circle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, from where you fired, you said. This was the position from where you could fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you then please indicate that part of your line from where you could fire, as you pointed at it before with the red pen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you now indicate the direction in which you would fire as you did before. I am just asking you to put down on paper -- yes, you can use the red marker and it is --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A felt tip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am just asking you to do exactly the same as you did before with the pointer, but now with the red pen. So indicate the directions in which...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I have to turn it around because it is easier for me to mark it then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Indicates] And perhaps it went like this, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You earlier indicated also areas more to the west.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. You couldn't see all of Sedrenik. Part of Sedrenik could be seen from these positions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, a few questions ago, some questions ago, Mr. Piletta-Zanin in his question said that the witness had earlier stated that the observation point had been taken, that is taken by the enemy. I don't recollect that and I have been checking the transcript and I can't find it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it has been said by the witness. I think it was -- I will find it for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for your precious assistance, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I asked you, before being interrupted, whether you knew anything about the type of weapons that you yourself had, you as an officer had?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I had an automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know what the range, the maximum range of this weapon is? I am not talking about how efficient it is but about the maximum range. What can you tell us as an infantryman?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well, I am not sure. It has been a long time since I was in the army. But we learned about this when I was young.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are not certain, but on the basis of your memory, give or take 10 metres, what was the range, please?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well, the maximum range was between 3 and a half and 4.000 metres for that automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thanks a lot. Witness, have a look at the map to your right, first of all. Can you see two red points, the first one is more to the north; the second more to the south, next to the numbers 8 and 3. Can you see these red dots?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, on the basis of your experience of these places, what is the distance separating point 8 from the red line that you have just traced which is further to the north, which is to the north-west?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: This line here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness pointed to the line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well, this map has been enlarged, but in relation to Bakija it is between 600 and 800 metres, as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... page 65, line 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. And again I am not sure which part of the red line to the dot the witness has in mind. Perhaps that could be clarified.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, the President showed the entire line that he has just traced, but we can ask him this question again. Witness, can you indicate the red line, the line that you mentioned very clearly a minute ago, could you slow us a red line, Mr. Witness, again?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There it is. The witness yet again outlined the red line that he indicated a minute ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, when there were exchanges of fire, as far as you know was it possible for there to be stray bullets?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I apologise for interrupting. There are a number of red lines on the map. For the benefit of the transcript, perhaps we could indicate that the red line is the one that passes through the red circle to point number 8.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That is the red line the witness pointed at. And, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I think the question you just put to the witness, we have heard that question before. Isn't that question similar like, "is it possible that it rains"?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... or perhaps the Prosecution. Is the Prosecution, is it the case of the Prosecution that stray bullets are impossible?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No. That is the case of the Prosecution, that stray bullets are possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So, therefore, it is of no use to establish again and again and again a fact which is not in dispute. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us what the colour of the uniforms used by the police was at the time, in general?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Blue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, do you know whether during the war --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I apologise if I have missed something, but which police? The police on the Serb side on the Bosnian Serb side, on the ABiH side?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When you were answering that question, how did you understand the question to be, police on your side, police on the other side of the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All the police forces wore blue uniforms in the area of the former Yugoslavia, almost right up until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To clarify things, both the Serb police and the Muslim police and the Croat police wore blue uniforms, that's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, as you were an infantryman, could you tell us with the human eye, as a general rule, can distinguish in relation to human person at a distance of about 800 metres, or in other words, what can one see when one observes a person who is at a distance of 800 metres?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well, that distance is too great. You'd see the silhouette of a person. It is difficult to make things out at such a distance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, at such a distance and I mean in general, would it be possible to distinguish, for example, a man from a woman with the naked eye, naturally?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: It would be difficult. It is impossible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, have you ever heard -- and I have to lead here, I think I may -- have you ever heard the name Dragonov?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever heard the name Dragonov or Dragunov?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, I would now like to go back to the issue -- to the question of orders that you may have ordered -- that you may have received when you were at your posts. So while you were militarily engaged during the war, while you were engaged in the military, did you and your comrades in arm receive orders regarding the manner of opening fire and regarding respect for the civilian population? First of all, could you reply by saying yes or no and then if you received any orders, could you tell us what the nature of these orders was.

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, we received orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Before moving on, when you said that you received orders can you tell us from whom you received these orders?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well, usually it was from company commanders or sometimes from the battalion commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us anything about how often these orders would be issued to you?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: It depended on the situation, on the new men who arrived. As new men arrived, we would receive orders, mostly because there were new men arriving in the units. This was an order to inform them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you briefly outline the nature of the orders that you received?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: We were ordered not to open fire at civilian targets; not to open fire if there were no provocations; only to open fire for defence purposes; and we were also told to save ammunition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. A minute ago in the course of your testimony you said that the enemy army had better weapons. What could you tell us about this matter? Could you be more precise? How did you know this, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well, this is something that I felt in combat because we were always attacked by forces that were stronger than our forces. And that's perhaps the result of fear, too, but we were shelled by the artillery for the most part. So they provided support.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it your testimony that the enemy artillery, the BH artillery was -- its presence was felt more strongly than the presence of your artillery?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I felt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you have mentioned artillery, and as you mentioned this a minute ago in relation to the photograph did you ever go to the Mrkovici village?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I slept in the Mrkovici village. When I was free, when I was on leave, then I slept in the upper part of Mrkovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, since you slept in the village of Mrkovici when you were on leave, did you ever observe when you were in the area of the village of Mrkovici, any kind of artillery unit?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In the area of Mrkovici the entire village, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, could you remind us of the period during which you regularly went to the village of Mrkovici?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well, mostly as we were on guard, this depended on the intensity of the attack. It depended on whether we would be there for 24 hours or 12. But on the whole, we would go home twice a week.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, thank you. But my question is as follows: You said that you went to Mrkovici, that you would go to Mrkovici, and I want to ask you how much time did you spend at these lines during this period, how much time did you spend at the lines that we have in front of us on the screen during this period?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: You mean -- you are referring to the entire period of the war?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. From which date up until when did you remain, did you stay at those positions?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I was at those positions from the beginning to the end, right up until the Dayton Agreement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And during that entire period you would visit the village of Mrkovici; is this your testimony?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, I would like to move on to the combat in April 1993. You have spoken -- you have spoken about this combat. I would like you to be a little more precise with regard to this fighting. When this unfolded in the second half of April 1993, when there was such fighting during this period, where were the men? Did they remain in the fortress? Were they positioned in the trenches, et cetera? What can you tell us about this?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In April 1993, there were men in the fortress. In the morning hours we were attacked again and the Sharpstone feature was taken. Two men died and the others withdrew. So on that occasion we lost the Sharpstone feature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, could you indicate on the map that you have in front of you where you withdrew from during this state of the combat? Could you point this out on the map?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: That's here. It is this part which leads to the Mala Kula, the small fortress, there is a curve here. This is where we positioned ourselves between the path and the house here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You spoke about 24 or 30 hours, but you said during the second half of April fighting continued; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, to the extent that you know about this, how many cartridges would you use in one day of fighting, the second part of April 1993, to be specific?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: It is difficult to say how many cartridge cases we used. There were sometimes five, sometimes two, sometimes ten. It was difficult to say how many loaders we used.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me what ten loaders for an automatic weapon represents in terms of the projectiles used?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Times 30.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you multiply the cartridge clip by 30; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. How many weapons did you have at these positions? How many men did you have at these positions in the course of the second part of April 1993?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In the part that was taken from us, we had ten men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. So if I am calculating correctly, that would amount to about 3.000 shots per day exchanged by these ten men; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, that would be in the course of the fighting when we were defending ourselves or when we were responding -- returning fire. That would be the maximum. That would mean there was fighting that was going on all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Exactly. I am just going to confer for a couple of minutes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we place the last photograph that we saw which bears the number 906. Can we have a look at that. That will be my last question, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That would be your last question is what I would like to know.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Are you referring to Exhibit D338?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I think we will have -- I need another ten minutes, Mr. President, but yes, that is the photograph. I apologise. We will take another 10 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's D338. If it would be possible to finish, that would of course be preferable, but if you would need another ten minutes, but then it would strictly be limited to ten minutes tomorrow. Please proceed. I mean ten minutes from now on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, a minute ago when we spoke about elevation 906, you mentioned a point that was about 15 metres from the vehicle. Could you point this out. Could you use your pointer to indicate this spot and leave it there.

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, is it correct to say that elevation 906 is the highest point of the elevation in question; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. But could you leave your pointer there, please. Thanks. Witness, if you move your pointer to the left, move it to the left, a little higher up.

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, stop. Can one see -- can't one see that the terrain here is a little more elevated than the point you indicated a minute ago; is that the case?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I think that we can stop there for the moment and we will carry on tomorrow with your permission. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but only for a couple of minutes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, exactly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will then adjourn until tomorrow quarter past 2.00 in this same courtroom. Madam Registrar, if I am well informed, same courtroom. May I ask you not -- you are supposed not to speak with anyone about the testimony you give in this court. So, therefore, no one, not to the Prosecution, not to the Defence, not to anyone else, and we'd like to see you back tomorrow morning, quarter past 2.00 in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
